newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATAVIO RUSSIAN DEBTS TO BE PAID BY SEPT 1.
newsitem.headline: LATAVIO RUSSIAN DEBTS TO BE PAID BY SEPT 1.

text.p: Transport Minister Vilis Krishtopans said on Monday that all the debts of former national carrier Latavio, which have stopped Air Baltic flying to Moscow, would be paid by September 1.
"My aim is to have the payment, worth $2.8 million, made by mid-August to September 1," Krishtopans told a news conference.
Russia is currently denying AirBaltic, just under 30-percent owned by Scandinavian Airlines, the right to fly to Russia due to the debts of Latavio.
The debt will not be paid from the state budget and talks are currently under way between AirBaltic, SAS and Riga airport.
"An agreement will be reached very, very soon," Krishtopans added.
Krishtopans was in Moscow on July 17 to take part in a meeting with Russian transport officials.
"The Russian position is that if you pay today, tomorrow you fly," Krishtopans said.
